zh: 十天以后，罗四姐接到了家信，罗大娘照她的话，是请乌先生代写的。这乌先生是关帝庙的庙祝，为人热心，洞明世事，先看了罗四姐的来信，心头有个疑问，何以回信要指写他来写。再听罗大娘眉飞色舞地谈胡雪岩来看她的情形，恍然大悟，罗四姐大约不能确定，胡雪岩会不会亲自来看罗大娘，所以信中不说信件等物托何人所带。不过胡雪岩的动静，在她是很关心的，既然如此，就要详详细细告诉她。她之指明要自己替罗大娘写回信，也正是这个道理。这完全猜对了罗四姐的心思，因此，她的信也就深副她的期待了。乌先生的代笔，浅显明白，罗四姐先找者马来念给她听过，自己也好好下了一番工夫，等大致可以看得懂了，才揣着信去看七姑奶奶。“七姐，”她说。“我有封信，请你给我看看。”“哪个的信？”“我娘的信，我一看信很长，当中好象提到胡大先生，我怕有要紧话在里头，不方便叫老马给我看。”“我比你也好不了多少，你看不明白，我也未见得看得懂。不过，不要紧，一客不烦二主，当初你是托应春替你写的现在仍旧叫他来看好了。”“七姐夫在家？”“在家。”七姑奶奶答说： “有个洋人要来看他，他在等。”
en: Ten days later, Luo Sijie received a letter from home. As she had requested, her mother had asked Mr Wu to write it. Mr Wu was the keeper of the Temple of Lord Guan, a warm-hearted man with a thorough understanding of the world. Reading Luo’s letter first, he had wondered why she had specifically requested him as the writer of the reply. Then, listening to Auntie Luo’s delighted account of Hu’s visit, he understood. Her daughter probably had not been certain whether Hu would call in person, which explained why she had omitted the name of the man carrying her letter and gifts. Yet his actions mattered greatly to her. Mr Wu must therefore tell her everything in detail: that was precisely why she had asked him to write. He had guessed her intention perfectly, and the letter fully met her expectations. His language was plain and clear. She first had Old Ma read it aloud, then worked carefully through it herself. Once she could understand most of it, she put it inside her clothes and went to see the Seventh Lady. “Seventh Sister, I have a letter. Would you look at it for me?” “From whom?” “My mother. It is very long, and Mr Hu seems to be mentioned in the middle. I am afraid there may be something important that I ought not to ask Old Ma to read.” “I am not much better than you. If you cannot make it out, I may not be able to either. But never mind. One guest need not trouble two hosts. You asked Yingchun to write before; let him read this one too.” “Is Brother-in-Law Gu at home?” “Yes. A foreigner is coming to see him, and he is waiting.”

zh: 于是将古应春找了来，拿信交了给他。他一面看，一面讲：“东西都收到了，胡大先生还送了一份很厚的礼，一共八样，火腿、茶叶、花雕……”“这不要念了。”七姑奶奶插嘴问道：“他信里称小爷叔，是叫胡大先生？”“是啊！杭州人之中，尊敬小爷叔的，都是这样叫他的。”“好！你再讲下去。”“五月初七胡大先生去看你母亲，非常客气，坐了足足有一个时辰，谈起在上海的近况……”讲到这里，古应春笑笑硕住了。“咦！”七姑奶奶诧异地问：“啥好笑？”“信上说。你母亲知道你认识了我们两个，说是‘欣遇贵人’。”古应春谦虚着，“实在不敢当。”“我娘的话不错。你们两位当然是我的贵人。”罗四姐问道：“七姐夫，信上好象还提到我女儿。”“是的。你母亲说，胡大先生很喜欢你女儿，问长问短，说了好些话。还送了一份见面礼，是一双绞丝的金镯子。““你看！”罗四姐对七姑奶奶说，“大先生对伢儿们，给这样贵重的东西，不过，七姐，我倒不大懂了，大先生怎么会将这双镯子带在身边？莫非他去之前，就晓得我有个女儿？”“不见得。”七姑奶奶答说，“我们小爷叔应酬多，金表杂七杂八的东西很多，遇到要送见面礼，拿出来就是。”“原来这样子的。”罗四姐的疑团一释，“七姐夫，请你再讲。”
en: Gu was summoned and given the letter. He read and explained as he went. “Everything arrived. Mr Hu also sent a very substantial gift, eight things in all: ham, tea, Huadiao…” “You need not read those out,” the Seventh Lady interrupted. “Does the letter call Little Uncle Mr Hu?” “Yes. That is how Hangzhou people who respect him address him.” “Go on, then.” “On the seventh day of the fifth month, Mr Hu called on your mother. He was extremely courteous and stayed two full hours, talking about your recent life in Shanghai…” Gu smiled and stopped. “What is amusing?” his wife asked in surprise. “Your mother says she was pleased to learn that you had met the two of us. She calls it ‘the happy encounter with benefactors.’ That is far more than we deserve.” “My mother is right. You are certainly my benefactors.” Luo asked whether the letter also mentioned her daughter. “It does. Your mother says Mr Hu liked her very much, asked all sorts of questions, and talked with her at length. He also gave her a present at their first meeting: a pair of twisted-wire gold bracelets.” “Just think, Seventh Sister! Such costly things for a child. But I do not quite understand. Why did he have those bracelets with him? Did he know before going that I had a daughter?” “Not necessarily. Little Uncle has so many social obligations that he keeps gold watches and all sorts of other things. When a present is needed, he can simply produce one.” “So that is the explanation.” Her doubt resolved, Luo asked Gu to continue.

zh: “你娘说，你说要回去，她也很想念你，如果你抽不出工夫。或者她到上海来看你。”罗四姐还未开口，七姑奶奶先就喊了出来，“来嘛！”她说，“把你娘接了来歇夏，住两三个月再回去。““上海是比杭州要凉快些。”罗四姐点点头：“等我来想想。”“后面还有段话，是乌先生‘附笔’，很有意思！”古应春微笑着，“他说，自从胡大先生亲临府上以后，连日‘庙中茶客议论纷纷’，都说胡大先生厚道。照他看，胡大先生是你命中的‘贵人’，亦未可知。”这话触及罗四姐心底深处，再沉着也不同得脸一红，七姑奶奶非常识趣，故意把话扯了开去，“什么‘庙中茶客’？”她问：“什么庙？”“关帝庙，就在我家邻近。替我娘写这封信的乌先生，是那里的庙祝，靠平常摆桌子卖茶、说大书，关帝庙的香火才有着落。”正谈到此处，洋人来拜访古应春了。在他会客时，罗四姐与七姑奶奶的话题未断，她也很想接她母亲来往，苦无便人可以护送。七姑奶奶认为这根本算不了一回事，写信给胡雪岩就是。“不好！”罗四姐只是摇头，却不说为何不好，及至七姑奶奶追问时，她才答说：“我欠他的情大多了。”“已经多了，何妨再欠一回。”“我怕还不清。”“那也有办法……”七姑奶奶想一想，还是不必说褥大露骨。罗四姐也没有再问，这件事就暂且搁下来了。
en: “Your mother says you mentioned coming home, and she misses you very much. If you cannot spare the time, perhaps she might come to Shanghai instead.” Before Luo could answer, the Seventh Lady exclaimed, “Let her come! Bring her here for the summer. She can stay two or three months before going back.” Luo nodded. “Shanghai is cooler than Hangzhou. Let me think about it.” “There is another passage, a postscript from Mr Wu. Quite interesting.” Gu smiled. “He says that since Mr Hu’s personal visit, the tea drinkers at the temple have talked of little else for days. Everyone calls him a generous and loyal man. Mr Wu thinks he might even be the benefactor destined to enter your life.” The words touched the deepest part of Luo’s heart. Composed as she was, she could not help blushing. With great tact, the Seventh Lady deliberately changed the subject. “What tea drinkers? What temple?” “The Temple of Lord Guan, near our house. Mr Wu, who wrote this letter for my mother, is its keeper. He sets out tables and sells tea, with storytellers performing. That is how the temple’s worship and incense are supported.” At this point Gu’s foreign visitor arrived. While he received him, the two women continued talking. Luo would very much like her mother to stay, but had no suitable person to escort her. The Seventh Lady thought that no difficulty at all: she need only write to Hu. “No, that would not do.” Luo kept shaking her head, and only when pressed explained, “I owe him too much already.” “Then what harm in owing him one kindness more?” “I am afraid I could never repay him.” “There is a way of doing that too…” On reflection, the Seventh Lady decided not to speak too plainly. Luo asked no further question, and the matter was left for the time being.

zh: 谈了些闲话，到了上灯时分，七姑奶奶提议，早点吃晚饭，饭后去看西洋来的马戏。罗四姐答应在她家吃饭，但不想去看马戏，因为散戏已晚，劳她远送回家，于心不安。“那还不好办？你住在我这里好了。我们还可以谈谈。”罗四姐想了一下，终于接受邀约。饭后看马戏回来，古应春也刚刚到家。“阿七，请你替我收拾收拾行李。”他说：“今天来的洋人。是德国洋行新来的总管。他说要专程到杭州去拜访小爷叔，顺便逛逛西湖，我只好陪他走一趟。”“怎么？”七姑奶奶高兴他说：“你要到杭州！好极，好极！你把罗四姐的老太太带了来。”古应春愣了一下，想到罗大娘信中的话，方始会意，欣然答说：“好，好！我一走办到。”他们夫妇已经这样作了决定，罗四姐除了道谢，别无话说。接着便谈行程，古应春计算，来去约需半个月。七姑奶奶便又出了主意。“你索性搬到‘大英地界’来往，我们来去也方便。”她说：“寻房带搬家，有半个月尽够了。”“嗯，嗯。等我想一想。”“你不必想。等我来替你想。”七姑奶奶是在想，有什么熟人的房子，或租，或买，一切方便，思索了一会，想到了，“老宓不是在造‘弄堂房子’？她问，“完工了没有？”“老早完工了。”“他那条弄堂，一共二十四家，算是条很长的弄堂。我想一定有的。”“那好。”七姑奶奶转脸对罗四姐说：“老宓是阜康的二伙，现在也发财了。是他的房子，只要一句话，就可以搬进去住。”
en: They chatted until the lamps were lit. The Seventh Lady proposed an early dinner followed by a visit to a Western circus. Luo agreed to dine but declined the circus: it would finish late, and she would feel guilty at making her hostess escort her so far home. “That is easily settled. Stay here. We can talk some more as well.” After considering it, Luo accepted. When they returned from the circus after dinner, Gu had just arrived home too. “A’qi, please pack my things. Today’s visitor is the new manager of a German trading house. He wants to make a special journey to Hangzhou to see Little Uncle and take the opportunity to visit West Lake. I have no choice but to accompany him.” “You are going to Hangzhou? Wonderful! Bring Sister Luo’s mother back with you.” Gu paused, then remembered the letter and understood. “Gladly. I shall certainly arrange it.” With husband and wife having decided between them, Luo could do nothing but thank them. They discussed the journey, which Gu reckoned would take about half a month there and back. His wife had another idea. “Why not move into the British settlement? It would be easier for us to visit each other. Half a month is quite enough to find a house and move.” “Let me think.” “You need not. Let me think for you.” She considered whose house might conveniently be rented or bought, and an idea came. “Wasn’t Old Mi building a row of houses in a lane? Are they finished?” “Long ago.” “There are twenty-four houses in that lane—a long one,” Gu continued. “I am sure some must be available.” “Then that is settled.” Turning to Luo, the Seventh Lady explained, “Old Mi is Fukang’s deputy manager. He has made a fortune too. If the houses are his, one word is all it will take for you to move in.”

zh: “看看，看看！”罗四姐急忙否定，“我想另外寻，比较好。”“为啥呢？”罗四姐不答，只是摇头，七姑奶奶终于想到了，在此她跟胡雪岩的关系，正当微妙的时刻，她是有意要避嫌疑，免得太着痕迹。七姑奶奶觉得罗四姐人虽精明能干，而且也很重义气交情，但不免有些做作。她是个心直口快的人，遇到这种情形，有她一套快刀斩乱麻的手法，是罗四姐所做不到的。“我不管你那颗玲珑七巧心、九弯十转在想点啥？总而言之，言而总之一句话，你搬家是搬定了。房子呢，或租、或典、或买下来，我来替你作主，你不必管。”罗四姐反到服帖了，“七姐，”她说：“我就听你的话，一切不管，请你费心。”于是七姑奶奶独断独行，为她买了阜康钱庄二伙老宓新造的“弄堂房子”。这条弄堂名叫富厚里，二十四户，望衡对宇，两面可通，七姑奶奶挑定的一户，坐北朝南，楼下东西厢房，大客厅，后面是“灶披间”、下房、储藏室。扶梯设在中间，楼上大小五个房间，最大的一个，由南到北，直通到底，是个套房，足供藏娇。另外四间，一间起坐、一间饭厅、两间客房，家具摆饰，亦都是七姑奶奶亲自挑选，布饰得富丽堂皇，着实令人喜爱。前后不过十天工夫，诸事妥帖，七姑奶奶自己也很得意。第十一天早上，派马车将罗四姐接了来，告诉她说：“房子我替你弄好了。现在陪你去看看。”一看之下，罗四姐又惊又喜，兴奋之情，溢于言表，不断他说：“太好了，太好了。只怕我没有福气，住这么好的房子。”七姑奶奶不理她这话，光是问她还有什么不满意之处，马上可以改正。罗四姐倒也老实说了，还应该加上窗帘。
en: “There, you see!” Luo hastily rejected the suggestion. “I think it would be better to find somewhere else.” “Why?” She would only shake her head. At last the Seventh Lady understood. At this delicate stage in Luo’s relations with Hu, she wished to avoid suspicion and leave no obvious sign. The Seventh Lady found her shrewd, capable, and loyal to her friends, yet also somewhat affected. A frank woman herself, she had a way of cutting through complications that Luo could not manage. “I don’t care what twists and turns that wonderfully clever mind of yours is taking. To sum it up, and sum it up again: you are moving. Whether we rent, acquire the house under a redeemable pledge, or buy it, I shall decide. You need not concern yourself.” Luo yielded. “Then I shall do as you say, Seventh Sister. I leave everything to you.” Taking full charge, the Seventh Lady bought her one of the new houses built by Old Mi, Fukang’s deputy manager. The lane was called Fuhou Lane. Its twenty-four houses faced one another across a passage open at both ends. She chose one facing south. Downstairs were side rooms to east and west, a large reception room, and, at the back, a kitchen, servants’ quarters, and storeroom. The stairs were in the middle. Upstairs were five rooms of different sizes. The largest was a suite running the full depth of the house from south to north, ample accommodation for a beauty in seclusion. The other four were a sitting room, a dining room, and two guest rooms. The Seventh Lady personally selected all the furniture and ornaments, arranging them with an attractive richness and splendor. Everything was ready in only ten days, and she was thoroughly pleased with herself. On the eleventh morning she sent the carriage for Luo. “I have arranged your house. Come and see.” Luo was astonished and delighted. “It is wonderful! I only fear I lack the good fortune to live in such a house.” Ignoring this, the Seventh Lady asked what she disliked; anything could be changed at once. Luo frankly mentioned that curtains were still needed.

zh: “窗帘已经量了尺寸，叫人去做了，明天就可以做好。”七姑奶奶接着又问：“你哪天搬？”“慢点！”罗四姐拉着她并排坐下，踌躇了一下说道：“七姐，说实话，房子我是真欢喜。不过，我怕力量办不到，房子连家具，一起在内，总要四千银子吧？”“四千不到。我有细帐在那里。”七姑奶奶说：“你现在不必担心买不起。这幢房子现在算是我置的，白借给你住，到你买得起了，我照原价让给你。”“世界上有这样的好事吗？”“你不相信，我自己郡不相信呢！”七姑奶奶笑道：“看起来，吴铁口的话要应验了。”罗四姐记得很清楚，吴铁口断定她要“做小”，如果“偏要做大”，就会“嫁一个克一个”。假使不愿“做小”，又不能“做大”，本身就会遭殃，性命不保。倘或如此，八字中前面那四个字的“财”、“官”、“印”，自然都谈不到了。所以只有心甘情愿“做小”，才会有福气。这样一想，七姑奶奶话中的意思，也就很明显了。话虽如此，罗四姐却不愿表示承认，可也不愿表示否认。这一来，唯一的办法便是装作未听清楚而忽略了她的弦外余音，故意言他。
en: “The windows have been measured, and the curtains are being made. They will be ready tomorrow. When will you move?” “Wait.” Luo drew her down to sit beside her and hesitated. “To tell the truth, I love the house. But I am afraid it is beyond my means. House and furniture together must cost four thousand taels?” “Less than four thousand. I have a detailed account. You need not worry about affording it now. For the moment, regard it as my property, lent to you to live in free of charge. When you can afford it, I shall let you have it at the original price.” “Can such good things happen in this world?” “You don’t believe it? I hardly believe it myself!” The Seventh Lady laughed. “It looks as though Wu Tiekou’s words are coming true.” Luo remembered them perfectly. He had insisted she must become a concubine. If she insisted on being a principal wife, she would bring death to one husband after another. If she would neither accept the lesser position nor occupy the higher one, disaster would overtake her own life. In that case, the Wealth, Officer, and Seal represented in the first four of her birth characters would count for nothing. Only by willingly becoming a concubine could she enjoy good fortune. The Seventh Lady’s meaning was therefore plain. Yet Luo would neither acknowledge nor reject it. Her only course was to pretend she had not quite heard, ignore the implication, and deliberately change the subject.

zh: “七姐，搬家是件蛮麻烦的事，恐怕……”“你用不着顾前想后。这里家具摆设都有了，你那里的木器，能送人的送人，没人可送，叫个收旧货的来，一脚踢。收拾收拾衣服、首饰、动用器具，不过一天的工夫，有啥麻烦？““我那班客户呢？”“这倒比较麻烦。”七姑奶奶沉吟了一会说：“我劝你也不必再做了……”“不！”罗四姐抢着说道：“不光是为我自己。人家也是养家活口的一项行当，我不能不管。”“那也容易，你找个能干的人，做你的替手。说不走，还可以要一笔‘顶费’。”七姑奶奶又说：“新旧交替，难免接不上头，老马可以慢慢搬过来。或者老马投了新东家，你就更加省事了。“听七姑奶奶为她的打算，简捷了当却又相当周到，罗四姐实在无话可说了，“七姐，我真服了你了。”她说，“如今只剩下一件事：挑日子。”“对。”七姑奶奶说，“到我那里去，一面挑日子。一面再好好商量。”
en: “Moving is a troublesome business, Seventh Sister. I am afraid…” “There is no need to worry about every possibility. The furniture and fittings are all here. Give away what you can of your old furniture, and have a secondhand dealer take the rest in one lot. Packing clothes, jewelry, and household utensils cannot take more than a day. Where is the trouble?” “What about all my customers?” “That is more difficult.” After a pause, the Seventh Lady said, “I advise you to give up the business…” “No!” Luo interrupted. “It is not only for my own sake. This is a livelihood by which other people support their families. I cannot simply abandon them.” “That is easily managed too. Find someone capable to take your place. You might even receive a payment for handing over the business. The change between old and new management is bound to leave loose ends, so Old Ma can come to the new house later. Or he might stay with the new proprietor, which would save you still more trouble.” Her arrangements were so simple and decisive, yet so considerate of the details, that Luo could find nothing more to object to. “I truly admire you, Seventh Sister. There is only one thing left now: choosing a day.” “Exactly. Let us go back to my house, choose a day, and discuss everything further.”

zh: 回到古家，略为息一息，七姑奶奶叫人取了皇历来挑日子。很不巧，一连八、九天都不宜迁居，最快也得十天以后。“那时候老太太已经来了。”七姑奶奶说：“我的想法是：顶好这三、四天以内就搬停当，老大太一来就住新房子，让她老人家心里也高兴，而且也省事得多，四姐，你说呢？”“话自然不错。不过，日子不好，没有办法。”七姑奶奶想了一下说，“有办法。俗语道得好：拣日不如撞日。撞到哪天是哪天，你说好不好？”“怎么撞法？”“以老太太到上海的那天，就算你撞到的日子。老太太到了，先在我这里歇一歇脚，马上进屋，你也把要紧东西先搬运了来，晚上摆两桌酒，叫一班髦儿戏，热闹热闹，顺便就算替老太太接风，不是一举两得。”罗四姐觉得这样安排也很好，便即问道：“七姐夫不晓得哪天回来？”“快了。大概还有四、五天工夫。”
en: After a short rest at the Gu house, the Seventh Lady had the almanac brought. Unluckily, none of the next eight or nine days was suitable for moving. The earliest favorable date was ten days away. “Your mother will be here by then. I think it would be best to have everything settled within three or four days, so that she can go straight into the new house when she arrives. It would please her and save a great deal of trouble. What do you say?” “Of course that would be best. But if the days are unfavorable, there is nothing we can do.” The Seventh Lady thought for a moment. “Yes, there is. As the saying goes, better to take the day you happen upon than labor over choosing one. Whatever day comes our way will be the day. How about that?” “How are we to happen upon it?” “Take the day your mother reaches Shanghai. She can rest briefly at my house and then go straight to yours. Move your essential things beforehand. In the evening, give a dinner for two tables and engage a troupe of mao’er opera performers to make it lively. It will welcome your mother at the same time. Two purposes served by one arrangement.” Luo approved. “When will Brother-in-Law Gu be back?” “Soon. Probably in another four or five days.”

zh: 古应春回来了。使得罗四姐深感意外的是：她的母亲没有来，倒是乌先生来了。那乌先生有五十多岁，身材矮胖，满头白发，长一个酒糟鼻子，形容古怪，但那双眼睛极好，看人时，眼中两道光芒射过来，能把人吸引住，自然而然地觉得此人可亲且可信赖，因此，七姑奶奶一会便对他有好感。在古应春引见以后，自然有一番客套，七姑奶奶问到罗四姐的母亲何以不来，乌先生乘机道明了来意。“罗四姐的娘因天气大热，又是吃‘观音素’，到上海来作客，种种不方便，所以不来。不过她娘倒有几句要紧话，要我私下限她说，所以沾古先生的光，携带我到上海来开开眼界。”“蛮好，蛮好。”七姑奶奶说：“罗四姐，我跟她一见如故，感情象亲姐妹一样，乌先生是她敬重的人，到了这里，一切不必客气。现在，乌先生看，是把罗四姐接了来呢？还是你去看她。”“她娘还有点吃的、用的东西给罗四姐，还是我去好了。”“那么，我来送你去。”“不敢当，不敢当，决不敢当。”“乌先生，你不要客气。为啥要我亲自送你去呢？这有两个缘故。”说到这里，七姑奶奶转眼看着丈夫说：“你恐怕还不晓得，罗四姐搬家了，是老窗的房子，我一手替她料理的。““好快！”古应春说了这一句，便又对乌先生说：“罗四姐的新居在哪里，我都不知道，那就非内人送你去不可了。”“我送了乌先生去，顺便约一约罗四姐，今天晚上替乌先生接风，请她作陪。”听得这么说，乌先生除了一再道谢以外，再无别话，于是舍车坐轿，一起到了罗四姐那里。七姑奶奶把人带到，又约好罗四姐晚上陪乌先生来吃饭，随即匆匆忙忙赶回家，因为她急于要听古应春谈此行的经过。
en: Gu returned, but to Luo’s astonishment, her mother had not come. Mr Wu had arrived instead. He was in his fifties, short and stout, with a head of white hair and a red, bulbous nose. His features were odd, but his eyes were excellent. Their penetrating brightness held anyone he looked at and naturally inspired both affection and trust. The Seventh Lady took to him at once. After Gu’s introductions and the customary courtesies, she asked why Luo’s mother had not come. Mr Wu used the question to explain his visit. “The weather is very hot, and her mother is observing a vegetarian fast for Guanyin. A visit to Shanghai would be inconvenient in several ways. But she has some important things she wants me to tell her daughter privately. Thanks to Mr Gu, I have been brought along to broaden my experience of Shanghai.” “Excellent. Sister Luo and I became close at once, like true sisters. Since you are someone she respects, please stand on no ceremony here. Shall we send for her, or would you prefer to call on her?” “Her mother has sent a few things to eat and use. I had better take them to her.” “Then I shall take you.” He protested repeatedly that he could not accept such an honor. “There is no need for formality. I have two reasons for taking you myself.” She turned to her husband. “You probably haven’t heard that Sister Luo has moved. Into Old Mi’s house. I arranged everything.” “So quickly!” Gu turned to Mr Wu. “I don’t even know where her new home is. My wife really must take you.” “And while I am there, I can invite her to accompany you to dinner tonight, when we welcome you properly.” Mr Wu could only keep thanking her. They took sedan chairs instead of the carriage and went to Luo’s house. After delivering him and arranging for them both to come to dinner, the Seventh Lady hurried home, eager to hear Gu’s account of the journey.

zh: “他是女家的‘大冰老爷’……”原来胡雪岩一回杭州，略得清闲，便与老母妻子谈罗四姐的事。本来娶小纳妾，胡雪岩原是自己可以做主的，但罗四姐的情形不同，好些有关系的事，都要预先谈好，最要紧的，第一是虚名，第二是实权。杭州官宦人家的妾侍，初进门称“新姑娘，一年半载亲党熟悉了，才会称姓，假如姓罗，便叫”罗姑娘“，三年玉载以后，才换称”姨奶奶“的称呼。至于熬到”姨太太“总要进入中年，儿女成长以后。可是胡雪岩却为罗四姐提出要求，一进门就要称”太太“。“那么，”胡老太太问道：“你的元配呢？这个也是‘太太’，那个也是‘太太’，到底是叫哪个？”“一个叫‘二太太，好了。”胡老太太沉吟了一会道：“她怎么说呢？”胡老太太用手遥指，这“地”是指胡太太。“我还没有跟她谈到这上头。先要娘准了，我再跟她去说。”胡老太太知道，媳妇贤惠而软弱，即使心里不愿，亦不会公然反对，但她作为一家之主，却不能不顾家规，所以一时不便轻许，只说：“我要好好儿想一想，总要在台面上说得过去才可以。”“台而上是说得过去的。为啥呢”胡雪岩正好谈“实权”，他说：“目下这种场面，里头不能没有一个人来‘抓总’，媳妇太老实，身子又不好。以至于好些事，还要老太太来操劳，做儿子的心里不安。再说句老实话，外头的情形，老太太并不清楚，有时候想操心，也无从着力。我想来想去，只有把罗四姐讨了来当家。既然当家，不能没有名分，这是所谓‘从权办理’。台面上说得过去的。“
en: “He is the bride’s matchmaker…” Soon after returning to Hangzhou, Hu had found time to discuss Luo with his mother and wife. Ordinarily, he could decide for himself to take a concubine, but Luo’s circumstances were different. Several consequential matters had to be settled beforehand, above all her title and her actual authority. In Hangzhou official households, a concubine was first called the New Miss. After six months or a year, when relatives and friends knew her, her surname would be used: Miss Luo, for instance. Several years might pass before she became yinainai, or Auntie. The more dignified title yitaitai, or Aunt-Madam, generally came only in middle age, after her children had grown. Hu, however, requested that Luo be addressed as Madam from the moment she entered the household. “Then what of your principal wife?” Old Madam Hu asked. “One is Madam and the other is Madam. How is anyone to know which is meant?” “Call one of them Second Madam.” His mother considered this. “What does she say?” She pointed vaguely in his wife’s direction. “I haven’t discussed that part with her yet. I wanted your approval before speaking to her.” Old Madam Hu knew her daughter-in-law was kind and weak. Even if reluctant, she would not openly oppose him. As head of the family, however, she herself had to consider its rules and could not agree lightly. “I must think carefully. Whatever we do must be defensible before others.” “It is defensible.” This gave Hu his opening to discuss authority. “With the establishment we now maintain, someone must take overall charge indoors. Your daughter-in-law is too unassertive, and her health is poor. You still have to attend to so much, which makes me feel a failure as a son. To be frank, you don’t fully understand affairs outside the house. Sometimes, even when you want to help, you cannot see how. I have thought it over endlessly. The only answer is to marry Sister Luo and put her in charge. If she manages the household, she must have the standing to do so. This is a special arrangement to meet the circumstances. It can be justified.”

zh: “你要她来当家，这件事，我就更加要好好想一想了。你总晓得，当家人是很难做的。”“我晓得。罗四姐极能干，这个家一定当得下来。”“不光是能干。”胡老太太说：“俗语说：”不痴不聋，不做阿家翁。‘做当家人要吃得起哑巴亏。丫头老妈子、厨子轿班，都会在背后说闲话，她有没有这份肚量，人家明明’当着和尚骂贼秃‘，她只当没有听见，脸上有一点懊恼的神气都没有？““这一点……”胡雪岩说：“我当然要跟她说清楚，她一定会答应的。”胡老太太大摇其头，“说归说，答应归答应，到时候就不同了。”她说：“泥菩萨都有个土性，一个忍不住闹了起来，弄得家宅不和，那时候你懊悔嫌迟了。”这是各人的看法不同。胡老太太以前也见过罗四姐，但事隔多年，是何面貌都记不清楚了，当然只就一般常情来推测。胡雪岩心想，这不是一下子可将老母说服的，惟有多谈一谈罗四姐的性情才具，渐渐地让母亲有了信心，自然水到渠成。
en: “If you want her to manage the household, I must consider it still more carefully. You know how hard it is to be the person in charge.” “I do. She is exceptionally capable. She can certainly manage it.” “Ability is not everything. As the saying goes, ‘Unless you can play the fool and turn a deaf ear, you cannot be the elder of a household.’ The person in charge must bear injuries without complaint. Maids, older women servants, cooks, and chair bearers will all gossip behind her back. Has she the generosity to hear an insult aimed plainly at her—like cursing bald-headed scoundrels in front of a monk—and pretend she heard nothing, without the slightest displeasure showing on her face?” “As for that… I shall explain it clearly. She is sure to agree.” His mother shook her head emphatically. “Words and promises are one thing; the moment itself is another. Even a clay bodhisattva has a temper. If she loses patience and makes a scene, disrupting the household, you will regret it when it is too late.” Their perspectives differed. Old Madam Hu had met Luo years before, but could no longer remember even her appearance and could judge only by ordinary human behavior. Hu realized that he could not persuade his mother all at once. He must tell her more about Luo’s character and abilities. Once confidence grew, agreement would follow naturally.

zh: 就在这时候，古应春陪着洋人到了杭州，谈妥公事，派人陪着洋人去逛六桥三竺，古应春才跟胡雪岩详谈罗四姐所托之事。以及乌先生代笔信中的内容，认为事机已成熟，可以谈嫁娶了。“我门老太太还有顾虑。”胡雪岩说，“老太太是怕她只能任劳，不能任怨。”“那么，小爷叔，你看呢？”“这要先看我们怎样子待人家，”胡雪岩说：“罗四姐不肯拉倒，如果肯了，她总也知道，我不能拿元配休了，讨她做大太太，而只有做小。做小称太太，又让她掌权，她只要这样想一想，就算有闲言闲语难听，一口气咽得下去，自然心平气和了。”“小爷叔的话很透彻。”古应春自告奋勇，“我来跟老太太说。”
en: It was at this point that Gu arrived in Hangzhou with the foreign visitor. After their business was settled, someone else was sent to accompany the foreigner around the Six Bridges and Three Tianzhu Temples. Gu could then speak fully with Hu about Luo’s requests and Mr Wu’s letter. He thought the time was ripe to discuss marriage. “Mother still has doubts. She is afraid Sister Luo can bear hard work but not unfair criticism.” “What do you think, Little Uncle?” “That depends first on how we treat her. If she refuses, there is nothing more to say. If she agrees, she must understand that I cannot divorce my principal wife to make her First Madam. She can only enter as a concubine. Yet if she has the title of Madam and authority over the household, surely reflecting on that will make it easier to swallow unpleasant gossip and remain at peace.” “You have put it very clearly. Let me speak to your mother.”

zh: 说当然有个说法，根本不提胡雪岩，只谈七姑奶奶跟罗四姐如何投缘，以及罗四姐如何识好歹，因为七姑奶奶待她好，所以言听计从，情如同胞姐妹。胡老太太很尊重患难之交的古应春夫妇，对七姑奶奶更有份特殊的感情与信心，当时便说：“七姐中意的人，一定不会错的。这个媒要请七姐来做，我也要听了七姐的话才算数。”一桩好事，急转直下，看来成功在望了。但古应春心思细密，行事谨慎，觉得乐观的话以少说为宜。“老太太也不要太高兴，人家肯不肯，还在未知之数。”古应春接下来细谈七姑奶奶陪罗四姐去算命，几乎与吴铁口吵架的趣事，当然，他决不会透露，这是他们夫妇事先跟吴铁口说通了的秘密。胡老太太听得很仔细，而且越听笑意越浓，“原来她有这样的一副好八字，看来真是命中注定了。”她接着又说：“这种人的脾气是这样的，要嘛不肯，要肯了，说的话，一定有一句，算不句。”“小爷叔，”古应春又想到一件事：“不知道婶娘的意思怎么样？”“她肯的。”胡老太太接口，“我跟她谈过了，她要我作主，现在，七姐夫，这桩事情，我就拜托你了。”
en: Gu had his own approach. He did not mention Hu at all, speaking instead of how well his wife and Luo suited each other, and how Luo knew when she was being treated well. Because the Seventh Lady had been kind to her, Luo listened to everything she said; the two were like sisters. Old Madam Hu held the Gus, her friends through adversity, in great respect, and felt particular affection and confidence toward the Seventh Lady. “Anyone Seventh Sister approves of must be sound. She must arrange this match. I must hear what she has to say before deciding.” Matters had suddenly taken a favorable turn, and success seemed near. But Gu was thoughtful and cautious, and saw little reason to encourage excessive optimism. “Please do not be too pleased yet. Whether the other party will agree is still unknown.” He told her how his wife had taken Luo to have her fortune read and how Luo had almost quarreled with Wu Tiekou. Naturally, he concealed their advance arrangement with the fortune-teller. Old Madam Hu listened closely, smiling more and more. “So she has such excellent birth characters. It really does seem destined. People of that temperament either refuse outright or, once they consent, keep every word they give.” Gu thought of another point. “Little Uncle, what does your wife think?” “She agrees,” Old Madam Hu answered. “I have spoken to her. She leaves the decision to me. Now, Brother-in-Law Gu, I entrust the matter to you.”

zh: “只要老太太作主，婶娘也不会埋怨，我同阿七当然要尽心尽力把这件事办圆满来。”于是古应春为胡雪岩策划，男家的媒人是七姑奶奶，女家的媒人不妨请乌先生承担。胡雪岩自然同意，便发了一份请帖，请乌先生吃饭。这在乌先生自有受宠若惊之感，准时到胡家来赴宴。做主人的介绍了古应春与其他的陪客，敬过一杯酒，托辞先离席了。席间闲谈，不及正事，饭罢到客座喝茶，古应春才将乌先生邀到一边，笑着说道：“乌先生，你我神交已久。”乌先生愕然，及至古应春提到彼此为罗四姐一家代笔的事，乌先生方始明白，人虽初识，笔迹早熟，这就是神交，因为如此，一切都好谈了。
en: “If you give your approval and your daughter-in-law will not resent us, A’qi and I will do everything we can to bring it to a satisfactory conclusion.” Gu proposed that the Seventh Lady act as matchmaker for Hu, while Mr Wu might represent the bride. Hu agreed and sent Mr Wu a dinner invitation. Naturally overwhelmed by the honor, the temple keeper arrived punctually. His host introduced Gu and the other guests, drank a cup with him, and then excused himself from the table. Conversation over dinner remained general; the real business was not mentioned. Only afterward, over tea, did Gu draw Mr Wu aside. “We have been acquaintances in spirit for a long time.” Mr Wu was puzzled until Gu explained their respective roles in writing letters for Luo’s family. Though they had never met, each already knew the other’s handwriting. That was their acquaintance at a distance, and it made everything easy to discuss.

zh: “照此看来，事情已经定局了。”七站奶奶很高兴他说，“这乌先生看起来很关心罗四姐，不晓得他看了她的新房子，心里是怎么想？”乌先生等七姑奶奶一走，从房子看到摆饰，在他心目中无一不新，无一不精，想不到她如此阔气，只以有七姑奶奶这个初会面的堂客在，不便现于形色，怕人家笑话他没有见过世面，此时就不再需要任何矜持了，毫不掩饰地显出艳羡惊异的神态。“罗四姐，我真没有想到，你年纪轻轻一个女人家，会闯出这样一个场面来！上海我也来过两回，说实话，这样漂亮的帚子，我还是头一回见。”他紧接着又说：“古家当然是有身分的人家，房子虽比你的大，不过没有你的新，摆饰家具也比你多，可惜有细有粗，有好有坏，不比你的整齐。”听他这样夸赞，罗四姐心里有种说不出的舒服，人生得意之事，无过于从小相亲的熟人，看到此人肯争气、有出息，青云直上，乱目相看。她此时的心情，亦大有衣锦还乡之感，不过紧接着而来的感觉，却是美中不足的空虚。“房子、家具都不是我的，我哪里就到得了能这样子摆场面的地步？”
en: “Then the matter is settled!” the Seventh Lady said happily. “Mr Wu seems very concerned about Sister Luo. I wonder what he thinks of her new house.” Once she had left him there, Mr Wu had examined the house and its furnishings. Everything seemed new and exquisite. He had not imagined that Luo was so wealthy. With a woman he had only just met present, he had concealed his reaction for fear of appearing ignorant of the world. Now restraint was unnecessary, and his admiration and amazement showed without disguise. “I never expected a young woman like you to establish herself so splendidly. I have visited Shanghai twice before, but this is the first house of such beauty I have seen. The Gus are plainly people of standing. Their house is larger, but not as new. They have more furnishings, but fine pieces are mixed with ordinary ones, good with bad. Yours are so consistent throughout.” His praise gave Luo an indescribable pleasure. Few satisfactions could equal being seen by someone who had known one from childhood as a person of ambition and achievement, risen far enough to deserve new respect. She felt almost as though she had returned home in glory. Yet an emptiness followed: the glory was incomplete. “Neither house nor furniture is mine. How could I have risen far enough to maintain such a display?”

zh: 这话在乌先生并不觉得全然意外，略想一想说道：“就算是胡大先生替你置的，即使用了，就算是你的了。”“也不是他，是七姑奶奶的。”“七姑奶奶？”乌先生诧异，“你们罗家哪里跑出来这样一位姑奶奶？”“乌先生你缠到哪里去了？”罗四姐笑道：“就是古太太，娘家姓尤，行七，大家都叫她七姑奶奶，我叫她七姐。”“啊，啊，原来是她。”乌先生眨着眼想，越想越糊涂，“那么，古家两夫妇，怎么叫胡大先生‘小爷叔’？上海人叫叔叔叫‘爷叔’，胡大先生怎么会是他们的小叔叔？”其中有个缘故，我也是前几天才听七姑奶奶谈起，她的哥哥行五……“罗四姐告诉他说，尤五是松江漕帮的当家。尤五的师父跟胡雪岩是朋友，交情很厚，清帮中人，极重家规，所以尤五年龄虽比胡雪岩大，却尊他为长辈，七姑奶奶和古应春亦都跟着尤五叫胡雪岩为小爷叔。“照七姑奶奶说，松江的潜帮称为‘疲帮’。他们这一帮的漕船很多，是大帮，不过是个空架子，所以当家的带帮很吃力，亏得胡大先生帮他们的忙。为此，胡大先生在杭州到上海的这条水路上很吃得开，就因为松江漕帮的缘故。”
en: Mr Wu was not entirely surprised. “Even if Mr Hu bought them for you, once you use them, they are yours.” “It wasn’t he. They belong to the Seventh Lady.” “The Seventh Lady? Where did such a married aunt suddenly appear in your Luo family?” Luo laughed. “How have you got so confused? I mean Mrs Gu. Her maiden name is You, and she is seventh in her family. Everyone calls her the Seventh Lady; I call her Seventh Sister.” “Ah, so it is she.” The more he thought, the more confused he became. “Then why do the Gus call Mr Hu Little Uncle? Shanghai people use that word for an uncle. How can he be their young uncle?” Luo explained what she herself had learned only days before. The Seventh Lady’s brother, You Laowu, led the Songjiang Grain Transport Brotherhood. His master was Hu’s close friend. The Green Gang placed great weight on its rules of seniority, so although You was older than Hu, he honored him as an elder. His sister and Gu followed his usage. “Seventh Sister says the Songjiang group is called an exhausted brotherhood. It is large and has many grain boats, but little substance behind the name. Leading it is difficult, and Mr Hu has helped them greatly. That is why he has so much influence along the water route between Hangzhou and Shanghai.”

zh: 乌先生听得很仔细，一面听，一面在心里想他自己的事。他虽受托来做媒，但仔细想想；不是什么明媒正娶，他这个媒人也没有什么面子，所以一路上抱定一个主张，如果罗四姐本人不甚愿意，或者胡雪岩的为人，在杭州以外的地方，风评不佳，那就说不得打退堂鼓了。此刻看来，自己一路上的想法，似乎都不切实际了。既然如此，就不妨谈正事了，“罗四姐，”他说：“你晓不晓得，我这趟为啥来的？”这佯问法，罗四狙不免有些发窘，不过这是自己的终身大事，不能因为羞于出口，以致弄成误会，所以很沉着他说：“是不是我娘有什么话，请乌先生来跟我说。”“是的。我原来的意思，你娘即使不能来，写信给你，也是一样，你娘不赞成。她的话也有道理，写信问你，等你的回信，一来一去个把月，倒不如我来一趟，直接问个明白。”“娘要问我的是什么话？”“问你对胡大先生怎么样？”这一下，罗四姐的脸有些红了，“什么怎么样呢？”她用埋怨来遮掩羞涩，“乌先生你的话，说得不清不楚，叫我怎么说？”乌先生在关帝庙设座卖茶，一天见过三教九流的人不知多少，阅历甚丰，不过做媒人却是第一次，因而有时不免困惑，心想，大家都说“媒人的嘴”是最厉害的，成败往往在一句活上，到底如何是一言丧邦、一言兴邦，却始终无法模拟，不想，此时自然而然就懂了，他在想：只要答一句：“胡大先生要讨你做小。”罗四姐必然既羞且恼，一怒回绝，好事就难谐了。“如果乌先生对胡雪岩的印象不佳，他就会那样说，但此刻已决心来牵这根红线，便要拣最动听的话来说：“罗四姐，胡大先生要请你去当家。”
en: Mr Wu listened closely while considering his own position. He had agreed to act as matchmaker, but this was not a marriage to a principal wife through the full formal rites, and there was little distinction in arranging it. On the journey he had resolved that if Luo was not particularly willing, or Hu’s conduct outside Hangzhou had earned him an unfavorable reputation, he would have to withdraw. What he now saw made those earlier reservations seem unrealistic. He might as well turn to business. “Sister Luo, do you know why I have come?” The question embarrassed her. But this concerned the rest of her life; she must not let reluctance to speak create a misunderstanding. She answered steadily, “Has my mother asked you to tell me something?” “Yes. I thought that if she could not come herself, a letter would do just as well. But she disagreed, with reason. A letter to you and a reply would take a month or so between them. Better for me to come and ask you directly.” “What does she wish to ask?” “How you feel about Mr Hu.” Luo blushed. “Feel about him in what way?” She covered her shyness with a complaint. “You are being so vague. How can I answer?” Serving tea at the temple brought Mr Wu into contact with every sort of person, and his experience was considerable. Matchmaking, however, was new to him. People always spoke of a matchmaker’s formidable tongue: one sentence could make or ruin a match. He had never understood quite how a word could save a kingdom or destroy it, but now the meaning came naturally. If he simply said, “Mr Hu wants to take you as a concubine,” she would surely be angry and ashamed, refuse in indignation, and destroy the prospect. Had he thought poorly of Hu, that was what he would have said. Since he had now decided to join the pair, he chose the most pleasing words. “Mr Hu would like you to take charge of his household.”

zh: 这话让她心里一跳，但却不大敢相信，“哪里有这回事？”她说：“大家都叫胡大先生是‘财神’，他家那佯子大的排场，我怎么当得了他的家。”“罗四姐，我劝你不要客气，你的能干，从小就看得出来的，胡大先生向来最识人，他说要请你去当家，当然看准了你挑得起这副担子。”看来不象是随口玩笑的话，罗四姐不由得问一句：“真的？”“当然是真的。没有这句话，我根本不会来。”乌先生说：“名分上你已经吃亏了，没有别的东西来弥补，你想我肯不肯来做这个媒？”乌先生的话说得很巧妙，用“名分上已经吃亏了”的说法，代替听者刺耳的“做小”二字，罗四姐不知不觉便在心里接受了。“你的意思到底怎么样？”乌先生催问着，“如果你没有话，晚上我就要跟古太太去谈了。当然，我是女家的媒人，一定会替你争。”“怎么？为啥要跟七姑奶奶去谈？”罗四姐问“莫非她是……”“她是男家的媒人。”“我娘的意思呢？”“你娘情愿结这门亲的。”罗四姐心潮起伏，思前想后，觉得有些话是连在乌先生面前都难出口的，考虑了好一会说，“乌先生，你晓得的，七姑奶奶跟我象同胞姐妹一样，我看，我自己来问问她。”
en: Her heart leapt, but she hardly dared believe him. “Can that be true? Everyone calls him the God of Wealth. With such a grand establishment, how could I manage his household?” “There is no need for modesty. Your ability was evident from childhood. Mr Hu has always been an excellent judge of people. If he asks you to manage his house, he is certain you can bear the responsibility.” It did not sound like an idle joke. “Really?” “Of course. Without that undertaking, I would never have come. You would already be making a sacrifice in formal status. Without anything to compensate for it, do you think I would agree to arrange the match?” His wording was skillful. In place of the offensive word “concubine,” he spoke of a sacrifice in formal status, and Luo accepted the idea inwardly almost without noticing. “What do you think, then?” he urged. “If you have nothing further to say, I shall speak to Mrs Gu this evening. As your side’s matchmaker, I shall certainly press your interests.” “Why speak to the Seventh Lady? Is she…” “The matchmaker for his side.” “What does my mother think?” “She favors the marriage.” Luo’s feelings surged as she considered it from every angle. Some things were difficult to say even to Mr Wu. After a long pause, she replied, “You know that the Seventh Lady and I are like sisters. I think I had better ask her myself.”

zh: “让我做个现成媒人，那再好都没有了。”乌先生说：“不过，罗四姐，你娘是托了我的，你自己跟古太太谈的辰光，不要忘记了替你娘留一条退路。”何谓“退路”？罗四姐不明白，便即问说：“乌先生，我娘是怎么跟你说的？”乌先生有些懊悔，“退路”的话是不应该说的。所谓“退路”是以罗四姐将来在胡家的身分，她母亲不会成为“亲家太太”，也就不会象亲戚那样往来，这样，便需为她筹一笔养老的款子，才是个“退路”。但看目前的情形，且不说罗四姐，即便是胡雪岩也一定会想到他那句话便是多余的了。因此，他就不肯再说实话，只是这样回答：“你娘没有说什么，是我想到的，养儿防老，积谷防饥，你要替你娘打算打算。”“原来是这一层！”罗四姐很轻松地答说：“我当然有打算的。”“那好，我也放心了。等下到了古家，你自己跟古太太去谈好了。”
en: “If I need only arrange a match you have settled yourselves, nothing could be better. But your mother has entrusted me with this, Sister Luo. When you speak to Mrs Gu, do not forget to leave your mother something to fall back on.” Luo did not understand. “What did my mother say to you?” Mr Wu regretted mentioning a safeguard. With the position Luo would occupy in the Hu household, her mother would not become a recognized fellow mother-in-law or visit on the footing of an ordinary relative. A fund should therefore be provided for her old age: that was the safeguard he meant. But in the present circumstances, surely not only Luo but Hu himself would think of it. The remark had been unnecessary. Unwilling to state his full meaning, he merely answered, “Your mother said nothing. It was my own thought. One raises children against old age and stores grain against hunger. You must make provision for her.” “So that is what you mean!” Luo answered readily. “Naturally, I have plans for that.” “Then I am reassured. When we reach the Gu house, speak to Mrs Gu yourself.”

zh: 为了替乌先生接风，古应春稍微用了些心思。乌先生既是生客，跟七姑奶奶又是第一次见面，应该照通常的规矩，男女分席，但主客一共四个人，分做两处，把交情都拉远了，而且说话也不方便，因此古应春决定请乌先生“吃大菜”。在人家家里“吃大菜”，乌先生还是第一回。幸好做主人的想得很周到，“吃大菜”的笑话见得多，刀子割破舌头虽是故甚其词，拿洗手指的水当冷开水喝，却非笑话，至于刀叉乱响，更是司空见惯之事，所以古应春除了刀叉以外，另备一双筷子。选的菜，第一，避免半生的牛排，第二，凡是肉类都先去骨头，第三，调味少用西洋的佐料。不过酒是洋酒，也不分饭前酒、饭后酒，黄的、白的、红的，摆好了几瓶，请乌先生随意享用。“乌先生！”七姑奶奶入座时就说：“自己人，我说老实话，用不惯刀叉，用筷子好了。”“是！是！恭敬不如从命，我就老实了。”乌先生欣然举著。“乌先生看见罗四姐的新房子了？”七姑奶奶有意将“子”字念得极轻，听去象“新房”。在她是开玩笑，乌先生却误会了，以为将来罗四姐会长住上海，她目前的新居，将来便是双栖之处。心想，如果是这样子，又怎么让罗四姐去当家？心里有些疑问，却不暇细思，因为要回答七姑奶奶的话，“好得很。”他说：“我听罗四姐说，是古太太一手经理的。”“乌先生，”罗四姐不等他话完，便即说道：“你叫七姐，也叫七姑奶奶好了。”“好！七姑奶奶，真是中帼英雄！”“怎么会想出这么一句话来？”罗四姐笑道：“恭维嘛，也要恭维得象才是。七姐又不是‘白相人嫂嫂’，怎么叫中帼英雄？”乌先生自己也觉得拟于不伦，便即说道：“我来之前，‘大书’说岳传，正说梁红玉擂鼓破金兵，‘中帼英雄’这句话听得多了，才会脱口而出。”
en: Gu gave some thought to the dinner welcoming Mr Wu. As a new guest meeting his wife for the first time, he should, by ordinary custom, dine separately from the women. But there were only four of them. Dividing the company would create distance and make conversation awkward. Gu therefore decided on a Western dinner. Mr Wu had never eaten one in a private house. Fortunately, his host had considered the difficulties. There were many stories of mishaps at Western meals. Cutting one’s tongue with a knife was an exaggeration, but drinking the finger-bowl water as though it were plain drinking water was no joke; clattering knives and forks were commonplace. Gu provided chopsticks as well as Western cutlery. He avoided underdone beef, had every meat dish boned, and used few Western seasonings. The drinks, however, were foreign. Instead of distinguishing between those served before or after food, he set out several bottles—yellow, white, and red—for Mr Wu to choose. As they sat down, the Seventh Lady said frankly, “We are among friends. If you are not used to knives and forks, use chopsticks.” “Very well. Obedience is better than ceremony. I shall be frank too.” He happily picked up his chopsticks. “Have you seen Sister Luo’s new house?” The Seventh Lady softened the last part of the Chinese word, making it sound like “bridal chamber.” She was joking, but Mr Wu misunderstood. He thought Luo would remain in Shanghai and her present home would become the couple’s shared residence. How, then, could she manage Hu’s household? He had no time to examine the doubt, for he must answer. “It is excellent. Sister Luo tells me you arranged it all, Mrs Gu.” Before he could finish, Luo said, “Please call her Seventh Sister, or the Seventh Lady.” “Very well. Seventh Lady, you are a heroine among women!” “How did you think of that?” Luo laughed. “Even a compliment must fit. Seventh Sister isn’t some adventurer’s wife. Why call her a heroine?” Mr Wu himself felt the comparison was misplaced. “Before I came, the storytellers were performing the tale of Yue Fei. They had reached Liang Hongyu beating the war drums to defeat the Jin. I heard ‘heroine among women’ so often that it slipped out.”

zh: “乌先生喜欢听大书，明天我陪你。”古应春爱好此道，兴致勃勃他说：“城隍庙的两档大书，一裆‘英烈’，一档‘水浒’，都是响档。乌先生不可错过机会。”“苏州话，”罗四姐说，“乌先生恐怕听不懂。”“听得懂、听得懂。”乌先生接着用生硬的苏白说道：“阴立，白坐。”大家都笑了。“乌先生不但懂。”古应春说：“而且是内行。”原来“阴立、白坐”是“英烈、白蛇”的谐音，是书场里挖苦刮皮客的术语，有的阴阴地站在角落，不花一文听完一回书。名为“阴立”，有的大大方方坐在后面，看跑堂的要‘打钱“了，悄悄起身溜走，名为”白坐“。由于彼此同好，皆有喜遇知音之感，大谈“大书”，以及说书人的流派。罗四姐见此光景，轻轻向七姑奶奶说道：“乌先生这顿酒会吃到半夜，我们离桌吧！”
en: “If you enjoy storytelling, I shall take you tomorrow.” Gu, a devotee himself, spoke eagerly. “Two performances at the City God Temple, one of Tales of Heroes and the other of Water Margin, are both celebrated. You must not miss the chance.” “They speak Suzhou dialect,” Luo pointed out. “Mr Wu may not understand.” “I understand, I understand.” In stiff Suzhou speech, he added, “Yinli, baizuo.” Everyone laughed. “He not only understands,” Gu said. “He knows the business.” The expressions were puns on Yinglie, Tales of Heroes, and Baishe, White Snake. Story-house patrons used them to mock freeloaders. Some stood furtively in a corner and heard an entire episode without paying a copper: “shadow standing,” yinli. Others sat quite openly at the back, then slipped away as soon as the attendant came to collect payment: “free sitting,” baizuo. Discovering their shared enthusiasm, Gu and Mr Wu felt the pleasure of meeting a kindred spirit and talked at length about storytelling and its different schools. Luo watched them, then said quietly to the Seventh Lady, “Mr Wu will be drinking until midnight. Let us leave the table.”
